meaning: Divine blessing and abundance as a sign of faithful rule
description: The number 7700 appears in 2 Chronicles 17:11, where the Philistines and Arabs bring tribute to King Jehoshaphat: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats. The context is that Jehoshaphat had walked in the ways of the Lord, removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah, and God blessed his kingdom with peace and prosperity. The double number 7700 – used for two different kinds of animals – emphasizes the fullness of wealth. The number carries a clear intensification of the symbolism of the number 7 regarding divine perfection: 77 multiplied by 100 unites the intensified number 7 with the connotation of abundance and completeness that the hundred holds. That this very number is linked to tribute from foreign peoples points toward the biblical idea that faithfulness to God leads to abundance and recognition, even from surrounding nations.

versions.meaning: The number 7700 has no well-established, specific symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: Even though the numbers 7 and 70 are highly significant in biblical tradition – where 7 symbolizes perfection and divine completeness, and 70 represents the totality of nations or a complete period of time – the compound number 7700 has no recognized symbolic role in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria). It does not appear as a meaningful number in biblical texts or rabbinic literature. One might speculatively interpret it as an intensification of the symbolism of the number 7, but this would have no basis in established tradition.
versions.reason: [major] The description lacks the reference to 2 Chronicles 17:11, where the number 7700 actually appears explicitly in the Bible. It is claimed that the number does not occur as a meaningful number in biblical texts, but it is mentioned in connection with the tribute paid to King Jehoshaphat (7700 rams and 7700 male goats). This is a factual error that must be corrected.; [major] The meaning field states that the number has no well-established symbolic significance, yet fails to mention that it actually occurs in the Bible. Although the number may not have a broad symbolic tradition, its concrete biblical occurrence should be reflected.; [minor] Footnotes should be used to elaborate on the context surrounding Jehoshaphat's kingdom and the theological significance of the tribute from the Philistines and Arabs, as well as the possible symbolic connection to the numbers 7 and 100.

versions.meaning: Divine blessing and abundance as a sign of faithful rule
versions.description: The number 7700 appears in 2 Chronicles 17:11, where the Philistines and Arabs bring tribute to King Jehoshaphat: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats. The context is that Jehoshaphat had walked in the Lord's ways and removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah, and God blessed his kingdom with peace and prosperity. The double number 7700 – used for two different kinds of animals – emphasizes the fullness of wealth. The number carries a clear intensification of the symbolism of the number 7 regarding divine perfection: 7 multiplied by 100 gives 700, and the combination 7700 (7 × 1100, or 7 × 1000 + 7 × 100) can be read as an intensification of wholeness and completion. That this very number is linked to tribute from foreign peoples points to the biblical idea that faithfulness to God leads to abundance and recognition, even from surrounding nations.

footnotes.text: 2 Chronicles 17:3–6 describes how Jehoshaphat sought the Lord and followed His commands, unlike the kings of Israel. His faithfulness is presented as the direct cause of the kingdom being strengthened and foreign peoples bringing tribute.

In a biblical context, tribute from foreign nations is a sign of God's sovereignty over all peoples. Parallels are found in the account of Solomon's wealth (1 Kings 10), where the queen of Sheba and other kings brought gifts as a sign of God's blessing upon Israel.

The number 100 is often used in the Bible as a multiplier signaling abundance and complete blessing (cf. Mark 10:30 about receiving a hundredfold). That 7 is amplified by both 100 and 1000 in the number 7700 can thus be read as an expression of an extraordinary divine gift.

Jehoshaphat was the fourth king of Judah after the division of the kingdom. His name (יְהוֹשָׁפָט) means 'the Lord judges/has judged,' which underscores the theme of divine justice that permeates the account of his reign.

versions.reason: [minor] Footnote 3 attributes the interpretation of 100 as a multiplier with reference to Mark 10:30 to a 'rabbinic' source, but the reference is from the New Testament and the reasoning is more generally theological than specifically rabbinic. The source should be changed to 'theological'.; [minor] In the description it states '7 × 1100, or 7 × 1000 + 7 × 100' as a mathematical explanation of 7700. Although this is correct, it is somewhat cumbersome and disrupts the flow slightly. The simpler form '77 × 100' could have been mentioned as the most intuitive breakdown, but this is a stylistic detail rather than an error.; [minor] The description mentions that Jehoshaphat removed 'Asherah poles', but 2 Chronicles 17:6 uses the phrasing 'the high places and the Asherah poles'. Both translations are acceptable, but it may be worth ensuring consistency with the most commonly used Norwegian Bible translation.
